GM Forgot a Part: 2026 Cadillac CT5-V Blackwings Delivered Missing Precision Package Hardware
12 photos
Photo: Cadillac
General Motors has issued a Customer Satisfaction Program bulletin, not an actual recall, because certain 2026 Cadillac CT5-V Blackwing examples equipped with the $18,000 Precision Package were actually delivered to customers missing critical rear suspension toe links. It sounds like an "oops" moment in which a GM employee failed to do their job.
The Precision Package is designed to significantly sharpen the sedan’s track capabilities by adding stiffer springs, a larger front stabilizer bar, revised suspension bushings, upgraded steering knuckles, and carbon-ceramic brakes to match the extra oomph.
However, it turns out that General Motors delivered cars missing critical components. A specific part of the $18,000 package was left out. Two rear suspension toe-link assemblies (Part no. 85829248) and four mounting bolts are missing. They were originally meant to be installed by dealership technicians during the Pre-Delivery Inspection (PDI).
These supplementary track-performance parts were supposed to be shipped loose, placed inside the trunk of the Cadillac CT5-V Blackwing sedan, upon delivery from the GM Lansing Grand River Assembly plant in Michigan, but were entirely omitted from the affected vehicles.
Photo: Cars and Bids Because these specific toe links are intended as an uninstalled, track-focused extra, General Motors' remedy does not involve taking the car to a dealership to have the technicians install them onto the suspension. Owners can have them installed at a service shop or ask the dealership technicians to do it.
The program is completely free of charge to affected owners and will remain active through October 31, 2028. Because the $18,000 Precision Package is a highly specialized, track-focused option, the overall production numbers are quite low.
This means that only a handful of early-delivery 2026 models left the factory without the aluminum performance toe links. The Customer Satisfaction Program bulletin affects just 11 units in the United States.
So what does the Precision Package actually bring? The Precision Package is a hardcore, track-focused chassis overhaul, designed for drivers who want to rock the track in their almighty Cadillac CT5-V Blackwing high-performance sedan, with no interference with the engine.
The package, however, completely changes how the car handles extreme cornering and full loads and costs $18,000 on top of the $100,695 starting price of the CT5-V Blackwing with the manual transmission or $106,970 when the automatic transmission is involved.
Photo: Cars and Bids For the money, it brings a stiffer suspension with increased spring rates, a larger front stabilizer bar, and heavily revised suspension bushings. New steering knuckles and rear suspension toe links, the parts that are currently missing from the trunks, are also on the menu.
The Magnetic Ride Control dampers, electronic limited-slip differential, and steering systems are uniquely calibrated to match the hardware, while the carbon-ceramic brakes massively reduce unsprung weight, delivering fade-free, mighty stopping power even under track abuse.
With or without the package, the engine specs remain unchanged. This means that the 6.2-liter supercharged LT4 V8 pushes out 668 horsepower (677 metric horsepower) and 659 pound-feet (893 Newton meters) of torque.
That is what pushes it from zero to hero (0 to 60 mph or 0 to 97 kph) in 3.4 seconds when equipped with the ten-speed auto box or 3.6 seconds when it comes with the six-speed manual transmission.
It runs the quarter mile in 11.4 seconds with a trap speed of 128 mph (206 kph) on its way to a top speed of over 200 mph (322 kph). Those numbers have always made it a formidable rival for the German sports sedan segment, like the BMW M5 or the discontinued Mercedes-AMG E 63.
